_doc: The asset contract (docs/explorations/2026-11-23-flexible-building.md). Every piece: its class, its fixed size in u (1 u = 0.6 m; the grid cell G = 2 u), its pivot (always the base centre of its front line), its front (+n: the piece's outward normal, toward the lower side or the street), and how it may vary. An instance the compiler emits must name a piece here and fit it; a model made for a piece must match it (tools/kit/fit.py).

edge.retain.straight.note: a retaining face with its coping; the face stretches to the drop, the coping never does

edge.parapet.straight.note: retaining face + coping + a balustrade section between two piers

sweep.parapet.note: a parapet section bent along a curve; any length in range

edge.steps.straight.note: a short drop (0.3 to 1 m) you can step over anywhere along it: treads of 0.15 m running out onto the lower side (the dais rings, a stoop)

arch.through.note: a level crossing water on arches, built to size by the renderer: from (x,y) to (x2,y2) along one face, depth to the other face along (nx,ny), n arches across the span, springing at low, the deck at h; the water (mat) runs on under it. No model: the renderer shapes it and dresses it in the painted stone (ashlar)

sweep.kerb.note: a kerb along a curve (a road a step below its pavement)

sweep.wall.note: a building's wall along a curve (the great hall's front)

joint.pier.note: between two parapet sections; turned to the bisector of the two

joint.newel.note: where a parapet run ends: at a flight's head or a building

joint.corner.note: a coping block where a retaining run turns; the two copings butt under it

connector.flight.note: a whole flight: treads and its two cheek walls with coping, sloping with the steps

head-flank.note: either side of the head, just beyond the cheek walls, on the top landing

foot-flank.note: either side of the foot, on the bottom landing

vignette.bench-planter.note: a bench between two planters, its back to the front's opposite side

setpiece.armillary.note: the courtyard's landmark: the armillary on its own round dais (two 0.5 m rings); one model

setpiece.bell-tower.note: the marker at the balcony road's west turn

setpiece.beacon.note: the marker at the balcony road's east turn

setpiece.pier-round.note: a free-standing round pier, set in matched pairs: gateways, gates, thresholds

setpiece.gate-tower.note: a square tower either side of a road's gate

setpiece.plaza-disc.note: the sunk plaza's radial paving, laid over its floor and ring of steps out to the rim: flagstone rings and seven coloured channels to compass medallions on the upper plaza

setpiece.library.note: the library on the middle terrace's west wing, its door toward the armillary (the whole-court paint-over)

setpiece.workshops.note: the workshops on the middle terrace's east wing, its door toward the armillary

setpiece.hall-half.note: one half of the great hall; two stand either side of the north road, facing the plaza

setpiece.great-hall.note: the great hall: two wings and a gatehouse whose archway carries the north road through it (pin p5)

setpiece.tree-oak.note: a broad oak for the woods (scattered)

setpiece.tree-pine.note: a tall conifer for the woods (scattered)

setpiece.tree-blossom.note: a violet-blossom tree, as in the concept (scattered)

setpiece.bush-gold.note: a yellow-green shrub, grown in code (lab/foliage.ts): every one differs by where it stands

setpiece.bush-pink.note: a shrub in pink bloom, grown in code

setpiece.bush-lilac.note: a shrub in lilac bloom, grown in code

setpiece.bush-white.note: a small shrub in white bloom, grown in code

setpiece.flowerbed.note: a stone trough 3 m long planted with flowers (pink, lilac, white, blue spikes), its back away from its front: stand it against a wall. Grown in code

setpiece.topiary.note: a clipped cypress cone in a square stone planter, grown in code

setpiece.tree-bloom.note: a small round-headed tree in pink blossom, grown in code

dress.urn.note: a gilded urn on a pier cap

dress.cap-lantern.note: a small gold lantern on a pier cap

dress.planter.note: a pot with a plant: 3 pots x 4 plants

dress.lamp.note: a street lamp: 2 posts x 2 lanterns

dress.banner.note: one cloth mesh with an emblem texture per element (textures/banner-<emblem>.png)

dress.bench.note: a stone bench facing a view

vine.ivy.note: a hanging leafy vine, grown in code (lab/foliage.ts) as wide as its wall section; without "grow" it is the painted strip, 1 x 3 m, cut to length

vine.violet.note: a hanging vine in pink and lilac bloom, grown in code

vine.grow-ivy.note: a long vine down a tall wall, grown in code to its longest path's length

vine.grow-violet.note: a long vine in bloom down a tall wall, grown in code

courtyard-formal.note: the courtyard's formal dressing, from the paint-overs

_doc_dress: Dressing (docs/explorations/2026-11-24-dressing-variation.md): pieces of class 'dress' are placed by a scene's 'dress' objects following a style in 'styles'. A rule puts pieces on sockets ('on' a joint piece, spread so none is within 'gap' u of another), at places ('at' flight-head / flight-foot, a pair) or 'along' road kerbs at a spacing. 'parts' pieces pick one of each part per instance; 'vary' gives a seeded scale and tint per instance (scatters use it too).
